title: Wine Wimsey Review · Wed Nov 11
subtitle: Batch date Wed Nov 11 (ODD day), built Tue Nov 10 at 1:36 AM. 10 feed posts + 4 stories, volume/format test day 3 (5 plain + 5 character, no captions or first comments). Plain cards at queue positions 1,3,5,7,9; character posts at 2,4,6,8,10. Characters: Hot Mess 2 (#4, #8), Homebody 1 (#2), Bold One 1 (#6), Settled One 1 (#10); stories Hot Mess, Homebody, Bold One, Settled One. Seasonal: 4 of 10 feed (plain #1 heated seat, plain #9 Thanksgiving ice; character #2 candle/early dark, #6 Thanksgiving sister) plus story 4 (scarf and hat for the mail); no weekday references, nothing dated. Quote sourcing: inbox 0 (no new items), plain cards 2 spun from FFF winners (#3 kindness/smoke detector, #7 frozen peas) + 3 original (#1, #5, #9); all 5 character quotes and 4 story quotes original. Credits: 9 new images x ~45 = ~408; plain cards use none. FLAGS: (1) Only 2 spun plain cards, not 3: the remaining FFF winners were already spun in earlier batches (patience, phone rabbit hole, premium adulthood, menopause hot/cold, bladder, hit-and-run, goatee, comebacks, whatever-I-came-for, spinach, the lied-about-where-I-was/Dana's house one), so I did not repeat them. #3 echoes the Nov 9-10 'fire department' stuffing line only loosely (kindness + burnt pan), swap if too close. #7 is the injured-by-something-harmless joke in a new detail (peas); similar idea to earlier sneeze/neck lines. (2) Cats were added by the model to #2, #10 (not asked for); harmless. (3) Every image viewed, each quote matches word for word, no stray logos. Alt text on every image post and story.

posts.quote: I turned on the heated seat at 6 a.m. and sat in the driveway for ten minutes. I wasn't late. I was at the spa.
posts.alt: Plain off-white card with dark bold text. Text reads: I turned on the heated seat at 6 a.m. and sat in the driveway for ten minutes. I wasn't late. I was at the spa.

posts.quote: I LIT THE PINE CANDLE AT 4:30 AND STARTED A MOVIE I'VE ALREADY SEEN. BY FIVE O'CLOCK I'D CANCELLED THE REST OF THE DAY.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a full-figured woman with short mauve-pink curls in a mustard fairisle sweater, lavender pants and pink slippers, reclined in a floral armchair with a glass of red wine, a lit green candle beside her, a dark evening window and a sleeping cat nearby. Text at the top reads: I lit the pine candle at 4:30 and started a movie I've already seen. By five o'clock I'd cancelled the rest of the day.

posts.quote: I try to brighten someone's day every day. Mostly with kindness. Sometimes with a smoke detector and a pan I forgot.
posts.alt: Plain off-white card with dark bold text. Text reads: I try to brighten someone's day every day. Mostly with kindness. Sometimes with a smoke detector and a pan I forgot.

posts.quote: I STOOD UP FROM THE COUCH AND SOMETHING CRACKED. I LOOKED AROUND FOR THE DOG. WE DON'T HAVE A DOG.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a grey-streaked messy bun and a pencil in it, wearing an olive vest and striped shirt, half-risen from a couch with a hand on her lower back and a startled look, glancing around the room, a glass of red wine on the coffee table. Text at the top reads: I stood up from the couch and something cracked. I looked around for the dog. We don't have a dog.

posts.quote: My daughter says I text like I'm sending a telegram. I wrote back, "STOP." She says that proves it.
posts.alt: Plain off-white card with dark bold text. Text reads: My daughter says I text like I'm sending a telegram. I wrote back, "STOP." She says that proves it.

posts.quote: MY SISTER ASKED WHAT I'M BRINGING TO THANKSGIVING. I SAID MY APPETITE AND ZERO OPINIONS. WE BOTH KNOW ONE OF THOSE IS A LIE.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a plus-size woman with a huge halo of auburn curls, round glasses and a geometric-print tunic, one palm raised and a glass of red wine in the other hand, in an autumn kitchen with a cornucopia and pumpkins and a phone on the counter. Text at the top reads: My sister asked what I'm bringing to Thanksgiving. I said my appetite and zero opinions. We both know one of those is a lie.

posts.quote: The fifties are a confusing decade. Last week I hurt my wrist opening a bag of frozen peas, then iced it with the peas.
posts.alt: Plain off-white card with dark bold text. Text reads: The fifties are a confusing decade. Last week I hurt my wrist opening a bag of frozen peas, then iced it with the peas.

posts.quote: I ANSWERED A VIDEO CALL BY ACCIDENT AND SPENT FOUR SECONDS SHOWING SOMEONE MY CEILING AND ONE CHIN. I'VE DECIDED THAT'S ALL I'M SHARING THIS YEAR.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a grey-streaked messy bun and a pencil in it, wearing an olive vest and striped shirt, at a desk holding a tablet up toward the ceiling with a startled open-mouthed look, a glass of red wine and a coffee mug beside her. Text at the top reads: I answered a video call by accident and spent four seconds showing someone my ceiling and one chin. I've decided that's all I'm sharing this year.

posts.quote: The group chat is assigning Thanksgiving dishes. I volunteered for ice. I've never once let anyone down with ice.
posts.alt: Plain off-white card with dark bold text. Text reads: The group chat is assigning Thanksgiving dishes. I volunteered for ice. I've never once let anyone down with ice.

posts.quote: I'VE STOPPED SAYING 'I'M SO BUSY.' NOW I SAY 'I HAVE PLANS.' THE PLANS ARE A CHAIR.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a slim woman with silver-white wavy hair and lavender glasses in a cardigan and joggers, barefoot in a green armchair by a sunny window with a book, a mug and a glass of red wine, a cat asleep on a blanket beside her. Text at the top reads: I've stopped saying 'I'm so busy.' Now I say 'I have plans.' The plans are a chair.

stories.quote: I TOLD THE PHARMACIST MY BIRTHDAY AND SHE ASKED ME TO REPEAT THE YEAR. WE BOTH DID THE MATH.
stories.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a woman with a grey-streaked messy bun and a pencil in it, in an olive vest, leaning on a pharmacy counter with a glass of red wine while a pharmacist counts on her fingers. Text at the top reads: I told the pharmacist my birthday and she asked me to repeat the year. We both did the math.

stories.quote: MY NEIGHBOR INVITED ME TO A THING. I SAID I'D TRY TO MAKE IT, WHICH IS HOW I SAY NO.
stories.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a full-figured woman with short mauve-pink curls in a mustard sweater, lounging on a green couch under a pink blanket with a phone on her stomach and a glass of red wine. Text at the top reads: My neighbor invited me to a thing. I said I'd try to make it, which is how I say no.

stories.quote: I'M NOT SAYING I'M ALWAYS RIGHT. I'M SAYING I'M NEVER SURPRISED.
stories.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a plus-size woman with a huge halo of auburn curls, round glasses and a geometric-print tunic, one palm raised and a glass of red wine in the other hand, smirking in a living room. Text at the top reads: I'm not saying I'm always right. I'm saying I'm never surprised.

stories.quote: I WORE A SCARF, A HAT, AND GLOVES TO GET THE MAIL. THE MAIL WAS ONE CATALOG. I REGRET NOTHING.
stories.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a slim woman with silver-white hair and round glasses in a knit hat, scarf, mittens and slippers, holding one thin catalog and a glass of red wine beside a mailbox on an autumn porch. Text at the top reads: I wore a scarf, a hat, and gloves to get the mail. The mail was one catalog. I regret nothing.
